rfm_tuples.R: 'Our Board and management are evaluating capital allocation priorities, including cash allocated to paying dividends. ... Financial conditions or our pursuit of strategic alternative uses of cash could lead to a reduction, suspension, or termination of the payment of cash dividends at any time.' (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors + Item 5)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify the soft 'evaluating' language against the actual dividend action taken between the 10-K (2024-02-27) and the next 10-Q (2024-05-08). Mode B — derive: 52nd consecutive annual dividend increase in 2023 ($1.74->$1.82) signals very high cost to break the streak; therefore the 'evaluating' language is forward-loaded.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2024 10-Q discloses: 'In April 2024, we declared a quarterly dividend of $.05 per share, a $.41 or 89% decrease versus second quarter of 2023.' The 2024-04-30 8-K confirms: 'determined to reduce our quarterly dividend... a decrease of $.41 per share versus the 2023 second quarter dividend.' Time from 10-K filing (2024-02-27) to dividend-cut declaration (~2024-04-30): 63 days. Claim evolution from 'evaluating' to 'reduced 89%' is large for that timeframe; the 52-year aristocrat status was broken.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honestly disclosed as a possibility in the 10-K, but the 'evaluating' framing soft-pedaled what was at the time a near-decided 89% cut. The 10-K language is calibrated to be defensible after the fact rather than informative on the date filed. Mode B finding: management already knew the dividend trajectory when filing the 10-K in late February given the March 22 credit-facility amendment that pre-staged the deleveraging narrative.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Effective March 22, 2024, we amended our credit facility to change the Leverage Ratio. The prior Leverage Ratio covenant required us to maintain ... a Leverage Ratio of consolidated funded indebtedness to trailing 12-month consolidated EBITDA ... of not greater than 3.50 to 1.00. Under the amendment, the Leverage Ratio covenant was increased from 3.50 to 1.00 to 4.00 to 1.00 for each quarter-end beginning March 31, 2024 and ending June 30, 2025. ... At March 31, 2024, we were in compliance with all of its debt covenants.' (Q1 2024 10-Q Note H)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify amendment terms and the 'in compliance' framing. Mode B — derive: if 3.50x covenant were comfortably met, no amendment would be needed; the amendment magnitude (3.50->4.00 = +14%) and duration (5 quarters of relief) is a measure of how close to breach LEG actually was.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Q1 2024 10-Q Note H (Credit Facility Amendment) + 10-K Long-Term Debt section
rfm_tuples.M_value: Amendment signed 2024-03-22 — 23 days after 10-K filing. Total debt at YE2023 was $1.988B; 2023 EBIT of $(90)M (negative) means GAAP leverage uses adjusted EBITDA. The covenant snap-back to 3.50x for Q3 2025 onward signals lender expects normalization within ~5 quarters — a tighter window than management's restructuring plan completion timeline ('substantially complete by end of 2025'). 'In compliance' is technically true only because of the amendment.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Textbook distressed-credit signal: a covenant relief amendment was negotiated 23 days after the 10-K, indicating distress was active during the 10-K drafting window but the 10-K did not pre-disclose the amendment as a foreseeable need. The 10-K Risk Factors only said 'compliance with our leverage ratio under our credit agreement' was a constraint on dividends — they did not flag covenant relief was about to be negotiated. Mode B: covenant amendments are forward-leading indicators of deeper distress.

rfm_tuples.R: 'We expect to incur restructuring and restructuring-related costs between $65.0 and $85.0 [million], of which approximately half are anticipated to be incurred in 2024 and the remainder in 2025. ... we plan to consolidate between 15 and 20 production and distribution facilities (out of 50) in the Bedding Products segment ... experience a reduction in annual sales by approximately $100 million.' (10-K Item 1A + Item 7)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify the Plan size ($65-85M cost, 15-20 facilities, $100M sales reduction) against the actual segment-level revenue trajectory. Mode B — derive: if Bedding Products trade sales already fell -17% in 2023 (from $2,356M to $1,965M, -$391M), the $100M Plan-related sales reduction is on top of an already-eroding base; ratio (100/1965) = 5.1% additional decline planned.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 1 + Item 7 (Restructuring Plan disclosure) + Segment Results table
rfm_tuples.M_value: Bedding Products: 2023 trade sales $1,964.7M (-17% YoY) with $444M long-lived asset impairment + restructuring plan adding -$100M to 2024-2025. Q1 2024 actual Bedding trade sales $448.0M vs $528.5M Q1 2023 = -15.2% YoY (deceleration not yet inflecting). Consolidated EBIT swung from +$485M (2022) to -$90M (2023, including the $444M impairment). Plan size ($65-85M) is only ~3% of FY revenue but the deeper signal is that 30-40% of Bedding facilities are being shut.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: shutting 30-40% of facilities in the largest segment is a balance-sheet capitulation, not a routine restructuring. The 10-K characterizes the Plan as proactive optimization but the simultaneous covenant amendment and dividend cut frame it as forced. The $100M sales reduction language understates the cyclical hole — Bedding was already down $391M YoY in 2023 and Q1 2024 ran another -15% YoY pace.

rfm_tuples.R: 'In 2023, our largest customer accounted for less than 6% of our consolidated revenues. Our top 10 customers accounted for approximately 31% of these consolidated revenues.' (10-K Item 1)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify the diversification claim against bad-debt language and receivables risk disclosures. Mode B — derive: if largest customer is <6%, a single-customer loss is not catastrophic, so the EBIT collapse cannot be blamed on customer concentration — it must be end-market demand (residential bedding) failure.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 1 (Customer Concentration) + Q1 2024 10-Q MD&A 'increased bad debt reserve'
rfm_tuples.M_value: Top customer <6%, top 10 = 31% — genuinely diversified for an industrial. However, Q1 2024 10-Q calls out 'increased bad debt reserve' as one of three drivers of EBIT decline (-29% YoY to $63M), implying customer-level credit deterioration is now showing through. No specific customer is named in the Q1 10-Q.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Customer concentration claim is verified and accurate. The diversification mitigates one tail risk but the appearance of 'increased bad debt reserve' in Q1 2024 is a Mode B signal that residential-furniture/mattress retailer credit is weakening across the industry — consistent with the Bedding segment thesis but not a misstatement.

rfm_tuples.R: 'We have served as the Company's auditor since 1991.' — PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, St. Louis, Missouri, February 27, 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify auditor identity and tenure via auditor_change_tracker (lookback 5y) and 8-K Item 4.01 filings.
rfm_tuples.M_value: auditor_change_tracker returned signal='CLEAN_AUDITOR_TENURE', n_8k_item_401=0 (no auditor changes in last 5 years), n_big4_resignations=0, n_disagreements=0. 33-year continuous Big 4 (PwC) tenure. Internal controls audit opinion is unqualified (no material weakness disclosed).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Auditor signal is strongly positive: Big 4 with 33-year tenure, no resignations/disagreements, unqualified ICFR opinion. This sharply differentiates LEG from forensic-pattern distressed names (e.g. AAP cluster with material weakness + CFO turnover). Verifies financial-statement quality.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Our $300 million senior notes mature in November 2024, which we expect to retire predominantly with commercial paper.' (10-K Item 7A + Long-Term Debt)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify the $300M maturity and the CP-roll plan against the commercial paper outstanding balance and the credit-facility headroom. Mode B — derive: refinancing with CP requires the leverage covenant to permit borrowing under the backstop revolver; the simultaneous covenant amendment 23 days later is consistent with making the CP refinancing legally feasible.
rfm_tuples.M_value: $300M 3.80% Senior Notes Due 2024 mature November 2024. Cash and equivalents YE2023 = $366M (substantially all held offshore; ~$19M of US tax leakage to repatriate). Maturities range 2024-2051; total debt $1,988M. Q1 2024 10-Q confirms refi plan still CP-funded. CP backstopped by the (now-amended) revolver. The amendment was therefore likely a precondition for the November refinancing.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: the 10-K presents the November 2024 maturity as routine but the covenant-amendment timing (3 weeks post-10-K) plus 89% dividend cut plus restructuring impairments make this refinancing notably riskier than the 'predominantly commercial paper' language implies. Domestic cash position ($366M offshore minus repatriation friction) is thin relative to the $300M maturity if CP market access dislocates.

rfm_tuples.interpretation: Strongly counter-signal to a 'lying / obscuring distress' read. The EVP open-market buy POST-dividend-announcement (price $13.39) is bullish insider signaling that the bad news is already priced and recovery is expected. This is the single strongest piece of evidence against a SHORT-tier verdict.

Cash from operations 2023 = $497M (up vs $441M in 2022 despite $90M operating loss — driven by working-capital release, not earnings). Total debt $1,988M; cash $366M; net debt ~$1,622M. This is NOT a balance-sheet distress story; it is a cyclical-impairment story plus a deleveraging-driven dividend reset. Honesty-alpha framework correctly identifies this as not-lying.

summary: LEG entered the cutoff with a severe optical drawdown (-60.3%) and broke its 52-year dividend aristocrat streak with an 89% cut, but the forensic profile does NOT support a 'lying-about-distress' verdict. Big-4 auditor (PwC, 33-year tenure, clean unqualified opinion), no going-concern flag, $497M operating cash flow funding both the $65-85M restructuring and net debt reduction, zero insider sales over six months, and an EVP open-market PURCHASE three trading days before the 10-Q dividend-cut disclosure together rule out concealment. The dividend cut, $444M impairment, and 3.50x->4.00x covenant amendment are all honestly disclosed cyclical-deleveraging actions, not solvency events. Mode-B finding: the soft 'evaluating' dividend language in the 10-K is mildly under-disclosed given an amendment was negotiated 23 days later, but this is a timing-of-disclosure issue, not a fabrication. Verdict: LONG-tier candidate — the honesty-alpha framework should keep this name (clean, just cyclically impaired), and insider purchasing into the announcement is the dominant tell.
